name: toggle-group
description: Single- or multi-select group of toggle buttons over native radio/checkbox controls, with roving-tabindex keyboard navigation and native l-model binding. A segmented style turns a single-select group into one track with a sliding thumb — the monthly/yearly switch of a pricing page — in pure CSS.

changes.note: A data-variant style group: default (the existing look, unchanged, and what a group without the attribute renders) and segmented — one filled track on the theme's button radius, equal-width items and a single raised thumb (the root's ::before) that slides under the checked item; the checked label is also semibold, so the choice is never told by the thumb fill alone. It is pure CSS over the native radios: :has() counts the items (up to six) and finds the checked one, so it works before and without the controller, and the keyboard model is untouched. Single mode only; a segmented multi group keeps the default look, an engine without :has() keeps the default per-item fill, and forced colours paint the checked item in the system selection colours. The default checked rule was also split in two so an engine without :has() still honours data-state="on".

Nested components keep their own parts. The stylesheet reached the items and controls with descendant selectors, so a component nested inside with parts of the same name took this one's styles. Parts are root > item > control, and the checked, focus and disabled rules ask :has(> control). Every part rule is now a child chain from the root, with the hops in :where(), so no rule changes specificity. No change for markup that follows the template.

The group now follows store-driven l-model writes. l-model sets a control's checked property silently, so data-state and the roving tabindex used to go stale (the checked radio kept tabindex=-1). The engine now announces checked/selected writes with a bubbling faqir:model event; the controller re-syncs on it and on a form reset, without emitting faqir:change. A plain script write (input.checked = x) is still not observed — use setValue().

data-state="on" / "off" on the items is now declared. The controller has always reflected every control's checked property onto its item wrapper (that is the whole styling hook — the real radio/checkbox is visually hidden), but the manifest declared no states at all. 0.8-10's undeclared-attribute rule now makes this class of drift impossible: an attribute a component's CSS selects on that its manifest never declares fails the registry gate.

item.description: One toggle button — a <label> wrapping a native control and its text; repeated per option

control.description: The native radio (single mode) or checkbox (multi mode) input carrying the option's value; visually hidden but the accessible, focusable, l-model-bindable control

label.description: Visible option text; provides the control's accessible name via the wrapping label

off.description: The item's control is unchecked. The controller reflects it on init and whenever a control's checked state changes, including l-model writes and a form reset; it is the default, so an item that has never been touched still carries it

on.description: The item's control is checked — the pressed appearance. The controller writes it; nothing else should

mode.description: single (radiogroup, one value) or multi (independent toggles, array value)

--toggle-group-track-bg.description: Fill of the segmented track (custom property, segmented style only). Pass a colour token.

--toggle-group-thumb-bg.description: Fill of the segmented thumb — the raised pill under the checked item (custom property, segmented style only). Pass a colour token; it is lifted by --shadow-sm and a hairline of --color-border.

required_attrs: role="radiogroup" on root in single mode; role="group" in multi mode
type="radio" on each control in single mode; type="checkbox" in multi mode
a wrapping <label> (or aria-label) giving every control an accessible name

keyboard.Tab: moves into the group to the single roving tab-stop (the checked control, else the first enabled one)
keyboard.ArrowRight/ArrowDown: move focus to the next enabled control (wrapping); in single mode focus-follows-selection
keyboard.ArrowLeft/ArrowUp: move focus to the previous enabled control (wrapping); in single mode focus-follows-selection
keyboard.Space/Enter: toggle the focused control (select in single mode)

a11y.notes: The controls are REAL <input type="radio"|"checkbox"> elements, so the platform provides the pressed/checked semantics and l-model binds through the engine's native radio (string) / checkbox-array (array) paths with no engine changes. Do not combine :checked with l-model on one control (two writers). The controller adds only roving tabindex, single-mode exclusivity for uncontrolled use, the [data-state] styling hook, and a faqir:change notification. Design note: multi mode uses native checkbox aria-checked rather than button aria-pressed specifically so array l-model works natively. The segmented style changes paint only: the thumb is a decorative ::before with no content, the checked item still carries the visible :focus-visible ring and the strongest text colour, so the selection is never told by the thumb alone. It applies to single mode (role="radiogroup") only; a segmented group in multi mode renders the default look.
